title: From Barren Land to Cricket's Premier Hub: How Jay Shah Built the BCCI Centre of Excellence
excerpt: The 40-acre Bengaluru facility has drawn Hardik Pandya as its first permanent resident and Bangladesh's cricket board for a study visit, but a fitness communication breakdown has put its sports science operations under review.
body:
• Jay Shah, now ICC Chairman, spearheaded the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, transforming 40 acres of barren land into one of the world's premier cricket training facilities in roughly 16 months.
  • The facility features three international-standard grounds, 86 pitches, a 16,000-square-foot gym, and a full sports science and medicine block with rehabilitation and recovery infrastructure.
  • Hardik Pandya has become the first centrally contracted Indian cricketer to make the CoE his permanent training base, relocating from Mumbai to target the 2027 ODI World Cup.
  • The centre faces scrutiny after a communication gap between its medical team and national selectors over Jasprit Bumrah's fitness forced last-minute squad changes for the Sri Lanka Tests.

When the Board of Control for Cricket in India inaugurated its Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru in September 2024, India cricket legend VVS Laxman — appointed as the facility's director — offered a striking assessment.

"I have been to some of the best academies in the world, not only limited to cricket, but other sports also. I have not seen this kind of facility," Laxman said. "The beneficiaries will be not only the future generation of cricketers, but also the current generation of cricketers."

"I have been to some of the best academies in the world, not only limited to cricket, but other sports also. I have not seen this kind of facility."

— VVS Laxman, BCCI Centre of Excellence Director

Built over 40 acres on the outskirts of Bengaluru, the Centre of Excellence — formerly the National Cricket Academy — was the brainchild of Jay Shah, then BCCI secretary and now chairman of the International Cricket Council. Shah drove the project from concept to completion in roughly 16 months, personally overseeing timelines with builders L&T, according to Laxman.

A Facility Unlike Any Other in Cricket

The sheer scale sets the Centre of Excellence apart. At its heart are three world-class cricket grounds. The main ground features an 85-yard boundary with 13 Mumbai red soil pitches, floodlighting, and broadcasting infrastructure for televised matches. Two practice grounds offer 75-yard boundaries with 11 Mandya soil pitches from Karnataka and nine Kalahandi black cotton soil pitches from Odisha, exposing players to the varied conditions they face across India's domestic circuit.

https://x.com/BCCI/status/2086377115868709036

The centre provides 45 outdoor net pitches organized into nine clusters, separated by safety nets sourced from the UK, alongside a dedicated fielding area and six outdoor running tracks. Its indoor facility features eight pitches with premium turfs imported from the UK and Australia, an 80-meter common run-up area, and integrated cameras for video analysis.

The Sports Science and Medicine block houses a 16,000-square-foot gym, physiotherapy and rehabilitation facilities, a sports science lab, and a recovery area with a jacuzzi, sauna, steam bath, underwater pool spa, and cold showers. A 25-by-12-meter swimming pool and an 80-seat meeting room complete the complex.

Pandya Makes It Home

Nearly two years after its inauguration, the Centre of Excellence has become central to Indian cricket's daily operations. In July 2026, all-rounder Hardik Pandya made an unprecedented move, permanently relocating from Mumbai to Bengaluru to make the CoE his full-time training base — the first centrally contracted Indian cricketer to do so.

"Hardik has already permanently shifted to Bengaluru. He has rented a property on the outskirts of the city, close to the COE," a BCCI source told PTI. "He will be the first Indian cricketer to make the COE his permanent training base for the remainder of his career."

Pandya, 32, has been battling recurring injuries, including a quadriceps problem that ruled him out of India's England tour. He sees the CoE as essential for extending his career through the 2027 ODI World Cup. He pays for his own net bowlers at the facility and works alongside both the CoE's support staff and his personal physiotherapist.

Growing Pains

The facility's reputation took a hit in August 2026 when pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah was formally ruled out of India's two-Test series against Sri Lanka. Selectors said they were initially told Bumrah would be available for at least one Test, but a reversal disrupted squad planning and forced the late inclusion of uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi from Jammu and Kashmir, according to Reuters.

The episode exposed a communication gap between the CoE's medical and sports science team and the national selection panel. CoE officials, including Laxman, held a virtual meeting with selection chair Ajit Agarkar to address injury management protocols. The BCCI has ordered a review of sports science leadership and return-to-play processes, with interim sports science lead Dhananjay Kaushik and team physio Kamlesh Jain now under scrutiny. The centre has operated without a permanent head of sports science since Nitin Patel's departure.

Global Attention

Despite the internal friction, the facility continues to draw international interest. Bangladesh Cricket Board president Tamim Iqbal visited the CoE in late July as part of Bangladesh's long-term plan to build a similar high-performance facility in Dhaka. BCB officials were expected to meet Laxman and study the centre's departments — sports science, biomechanics, rehabilitation, and player development programs, according to Sportstar.

For cricket fans in the Indian diaspora, the Centre of Excellence represents the BCCI's most ambitious investment in infrastructure — a facility Shah envisioned not just for cricket but as a broader contribution to sports science. Whether its operations can match that ambition is the question the BCCI is now working to answer.
image_caption: The BCCI Centre of Excellence was inaugurated by Jay Shah and Roger Binny in Bengaluru in September 2024. The 40-acre facility has become central to Indian cricket training and rehabilitation operations.
